per-resource request struct alongside that resource's own filter fields:

```ignore
}
```

Sort.description:
Standard sort inputs for admin list endpoints. Flatten this into a
per-resource request struct alongside `Page`:

```ignore
#[derive(Deserialize, ToSchema)]
pub struct ListThingsRequest {
    #[serde(default)]
    search: Option<String>,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    page: Page,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    sort: Sort,
}
```

`sort_by` is a client-supplied string, so a handler must NEVER map it to a
column directly — resolve it against an explicit allow-list with
[`Sort::resolve`], which falls back to the handler's default for any
unknown or absent key.

sort_by.description: Logical column key to sort by (must be one the handler allow-lists).

oneOf.description: Sort direction; defaults to ascending when a `sort_by` is given.

SortDir.description: Sort direction for a list endpoint.

SpRow.description: SP row for API responses. Never carries the private key.

private_key.description: Empty or absent leaves the existing key unchanged.

deleted.description:
Soft-delete action: `true` marks the account deleted (server stamps
deleted_at/deleted_by), `false` restores it. Omitted leaves it as-is.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete timestamp; null when the account is active. odo never
hard-deletes shared rows, so a deleted account stays resolvable.

deleted_by.description: Id of the user who soft-deleted this account (if deleted).

oneOf.description: Present when the user has a local (username/password) account.

deleted_at.description:
RFC3339 soft-delete timestamp; null for active users. get_user resolves
by id and returns soft-deleted users flagged so historical `*_by`
references still render (login/search stay active-only).
